title: Duality exchanges Alice's and Bob's conditioning variables
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$ and a hard-distribution sample $\omega$ with special coordinate $T \in \{0,\dots,n-1\}$. Write $\mathrm{rev}$ for the order-reversing map $i \mapsto n-1-i$ on coordinates, and for a Boolean vector $u$ write $\bar u = u \circ \mathrm{rev}$ for its coordinate reversal. Recall that Alice's conditioning variable of $\omega$ is the triple $\bigl(T,\ X_{<T},\ Y_{\ge T}\bigr)$ — the special coordinate together with Alice's bits strictly before $T$ (padded with $\mathrm{false}$ elsewhere) and Bob's bits from $T$ onward — while Bob's conditioning variable is $\bigl(T,\ X_{\le T},\ Y_{>T}\bigr)$. Let $\omega^\ast$ denote the dual sample, obtained from $\omega$ by reversing the coordinate order and interchanging Alice's and Bob's roles. Then Bob's conditioning variable of $\omega^\ast$ equals the dual recoding of Alice's conditioning variable of $\omega$; that is, if $\bigl(T,\ X_{<T},\ Y_{\ge T}\bigr)$ is Alice's conditioning variable of $\omega$, then Bob's conditioning variable of $\omega^\ast$ is exactly $\bigl(\mathrm{rev}(T),\ \overline{Y_{\ge T}},\ \overline{X_{<T}}\bigr)$.
replaced: Bob's corrected conditioning in the dual is Alice's corrected conditioning in recoded form.
